arxiv-2203-10733.title: Constraints on cosmic birefringence using E - mode polarisation
arxiv-2203-10733.creator: Arefe Abghari, Raelyn M. Sullivan, Lukas T. Hergt, and Douglas Scott
arxiv-2203-10733.description: Abstract A birefringent universe could show itself through a rotation of the plane of polarisation of the cosmic microwave background photons. This is usually investigated using polarisation B B modes, which is degenerate with miscalibration of the orientation of the polarimeters.

arxiv-2303-11111.title: Iterative Partial Fulfillment of Counterfactual Explanations: Benefits and Risks Conference: AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society; August 8–10, 2023; Montréal, QC, Canada AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES ’23), August 8–10, 2023, Montréal, QC, Canada DOI: 10.1145/3600211
arxiv-2303-11111.creator: Yilun Zhou
arxiv-2303-11111.description: Abstract . Counterfactual (CF) explanations, also known as contrastive explanations and algorithmic recourses, are popular for explaining machine learning models in high-stakes domains. For a subject that receives a negative model prediction (e.g., mortgage application denial), the CF explanations are similar instances but with positive predictions, which informs the subject of ways to improve.

arxiv-2307-05406.title: Measuring Trotter error and its application to precision-guaranteed Hamiltonian simulations
arxiv-2307-05406.creator: Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, Hideki Kono, Keisuke Fujii
arxiv-2307-05406.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, Hideki Kono, Keisuke Fujii. Trotterization is the most common and convenient approximation method for Hamiltonian simulations on digital quantum computers, but estimating its error accurately is computationally difficult for large quantum systems. Here, we develop a method for measuring the Trotter error without ancillary qubits on quantum circuits by combining the m m th- and n n th-order ( m < n m<n ) Trotterizations rather than consulting with mathematical error bounds.

arxiv-2402-03136.title: Mastering Zero-Shot Interactions in Cooperative and Competitive Simultaneous Games
arxiv-2402-03136.creator: Yannik Mahlau, Frederik Schubert, Bodo Rosenhahn
arxiv-2402-03136.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yannik Mahlau, Frederik Schubert, Bodo Rosenhahn. The combination of self-play and planning has achieved great successes in sequential games, for instance in Chess and Go. However, adapting algorithms such as AlphaZero to simultaneous games poses a new challenge. In these games, missing information about concurrent actions of other agents is a limiting factor as they may select different Nash equilibria or do not play optimally at all.

arxiv-2406-06342.title: A Guide to Stochastic Optimisation for Large-Scale Inverse Problems
arxiv-2406-06342.creator: Matthias J. Ehrhardt, Željko Kereta, Jingwei Liang, Junqi Tang
arxiv-2406-06342.description: Abstract Stochastic optimisation algorithms are the de facto standard for machine learning with large amounts of data. Handling only a subset of available data in each optimisation step dramatically reduces the per-iteration computational costs, while still ensuring significant progress towards the solution.

arxiv-2409-03621.title: Attend First, Consolidate Later: On the Importance of Attention in Different LLM Layers
arxiv-2409-03621.creator: Amit Ben-Artzy, Roy Schwartz
arxiv-2409-03621.description: Abstract In decoder-based LLMs, the representation of a given token at a certain layer serves two purposes: as input to the attention mechanism of the current token; and as input to the attention mechanism of future tokens. In this work, we show that the importance of the latter role might be overestimated for some layers.

arxiv-2501-19195.title: Rethinking Early Stopping: Refine, Then Calibrate
arxiv-2501-19195.creator: Eugène Berta, David Holzmüller, Michael I. Jordan, Francis Bach
arxiv-2501-19195.description: Abstract Machine learning classifiers often produce probabilistic predictions that are critical for accurate and interpretable decision-making in various domains. The quality of these predictions is generally evaluated with proper losses, such as cross-entropy, which decompose into two components: calibration error assesses general under/overconfidence, while refinement error measures the ability to distinguish different classes.

arxiv-2509-18057.title: Reinforced Generation of Combinatorial Structures: Applications to Complexity Theory
arxiv-2509-18057.creator: Ansh Nagda, Prabhakar Raghavan, Abhradeep Thakurta
arxiv-2509-18057.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ansh Nagda, Prabhakar Raghavan, Abhradeep Thakurta. We explore whether techniques from AI can help discover new combinatorial structures that improve on known limits on efficient algorithms. Specifically, we use AlphaEvolve (an LLM coding agent) to study two settings: a) Average-case hardness for MAX-CUT and MAX-Independent Set: We improve a recent result of Kunisky and Yu to obtain near-optimal upper and (conditional) lower bounds on certification algorithms for MAX-CUT and MAX-Independent Set on random 3- and 4-regular graphs.

arxiv-2512-00412.title: Red Teaming Large Reasoning Models
arxiv-2512-00412.creator: Jiawei Chen, Yang Yang, Chao Yu, Yu Tian, Zhi Cao, Xue Yang, Linghao Li, Hang Su, Zhaoxia Yin
arxiv-2512-00412.description: Abstract Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have emerged as a powerful advancement in multi-step reasoning tasks, offering enhanced transparency and logical consistency through explicit chains of thought (CoT). However, these models introduce novel safety and reliability risks, such as CoT-hijacking and prompt-induced inefficiencies, which are not fully captured by existing evaluation methods.

arxiv-2601-15673.title: ENHANCING GUIDANCE FOR MISSING DATA IN DIFFUSION-BASED SEQUENTIAL RECOMMENDATION
arxiv-2601-15673.creator: Qilong Yan, Yifei Xing, Dugang Liu, Jingpu Duan, Jian Yin
arxiv-2601-15673.description: Abstract Contemporary sequential recommendation methods are becoming more complex, shifting from classification to a diffusion-guided generative paradigm. However, the quality of guidance in the form of user information is often compromised by missing data in the observed sequences, leading to suboptimal generation quality.

britannica-1911-commemoration.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-commemoration.description: Article 'Commemoration' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. It is also the name for the annual act, or Encaenia, the ceremonial closing of the academic year at Oxford University. It consists of a Latin oration in commemoration of benefactors and founders; of the recitation of prize compositions in prose and verse, and the conferring of honorary degrees upon English or foreign celebrities.

pmc-10573211.title: Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Transgender People after Gender-Affirming Hormone Therapy
pmc-10573211.creator: Esteban Sánchez-Toscano, Jesús Domínguez-Riscart, Laura Larrán-Escandón, Isabel Mateo-Gavira, Manuel Aguilar-Diosdado, Arrigo Cicero
pmc-10573211.description: Introduction: In the last decade, healthcare for the transgender population has increased considerably in many countries thanks to depathologization movements and the easier accessibility of medical assistance. The age at which they request to start gender-affirming hormones (GAHs) is increasingly younger.

pmc-10657289.title: Principles of oncology taught in a one-week course
pmc-10657289.creator: Matthias Oettle, Marcel Büttner, Marie Forster, Laura Gajdi, Johannes Mücke, Alexander Nieto, Sonja Heuser, Johanna Huber, Franziska Walter, Stefanie Corradini, Maximilian Niyazi, Claus Belka, Martin Dreyling, Martin R Fischer, Daniel F Fleischmann
pmc-10657289.description: BackgroundGrowing challenges in oncology require evolving educational methods and content. International efforts to reform oncology education are underway. Hands-on, interdisciplinary, and compact course formats have shown great effectiveness in the education of medical students. Our aim was to establish a new interdisciplinary one-week course on the principles of oncology using state-of-the-art teaching methods.

pmc-12661303.title: Constructing dyadic management behavioral personas for patient-caregiver dyads in ambulatory chemotherapy: A qualitative study
pmc-12661303.creator: Tianze Yu, Xiaoju Zhang, Liying Wang, Zhenqi Lu
pmc-12661303.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop patient-caregiver dyadic personas in ambulatory chemotherapy settings. These personas will enable clinicians to rapidly identify behavioral heterogeneity in dyadic illness management behaviors and deliver targeted support and guidance.MethodsAn interpretive phenomenological study was conducted at a tertiary cancer hospital in mainland China from March to June 2025.

pmc-12748613.title: The Hungarian cross-cultural adaptation of the MMQL-AF for measuring quality of life in adolescents with cancer
pmc-12748613.creator: Márton Szabados, Nelli Farkas, Andrea Fleisz, Kata Takács, Orsolya Juhász, Márk Hernádfői, Brigitta Teutsch, Monika Csóka, Péter Hegyi, Miklós Garami
pmc-12748613.description: With improvements in childhood cancer survival, attention has shifted toward health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and long-term treatment effects. This study aimed to validate the Hungarian version of the Minneapolis-Manchester Quality of Life Instrument – Adolescent Form (MMQL-AF) and explore factors associated with HRQoL among adolescents and young people with cancer.

pmc-13156507.title: Synergistic effects of diabetic neuropathy and kidney function decline on second metatarsal skeletal health and foot function: a pilot study
pmc-13156507.creator: Victor A Cheuy, Saghi Sadoughi, Hasung Moon, Jalen Ellis, Rodney Gross, David R Sinacore, Mary K Hastings, Richard B Souza, Galateia J Kazakia
pmc-13156507.description: A discouraging increase in diabetes-related nontraumatic lower-extremity amputations (NLEA) has occurred over the last decade. Individuals with diabetic neuropathy (DMPN) and CKD are at the highest risk for NLEA. Despite the critical implications, little is known about the factors that initiate the cascade of events leading to NLEA, limiting early and effective interventions.

pmc-13211103.title: SLP-Net: A Dual-Level Contrastive Learning Framework with Stripe Attention for Elongated Pepper Detection in Complex Field Environments
pmc-13211103.creator: Jiangquan Zeng, Jiangzhang Zhu, Guoxiong Zhou, Peng Wang
pmc-13211103.description: Pepper detection in field images is difficult because the fruits can differ substantially in appearance, and many are partially covered by nearby leaves. Localization becomes less reliable when a pepper is slender or when only part of its contour is visible. SLP-Net was developed for this setting.

pmc-13346805.title: PMN-MDSCs-derived exosomal S100A9 drives breast cancer progression by enhancing cancer stemness and CXCL5-mediated metastatic potential
pmc-13346805.creator: Bo Wang, Binjie Su, Qi Cai, Tao Jiang, Weidong Liu, Xiaoguo Zhao, Yuekang Xu, Changying Guo, Jinyao Li
pmc-13346805.description: Polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs) represent a critical subset of immunosuppressive cells within the tumor microenvironment. Their interaction with breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs) constitutes a vital link that drives the malignant progression of breast cancer, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

pmc-13361271.title: Step‐Edge Functionalization by N‐Heterocyclic Carbenes Enhances Catalytic Activity in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
pmc-13361271.creator: Philipp Wiesener, Ankita Das, Elena Kolodzeiski, Duong Tran, Ying Pan, Harald Fuchs, Nieves López‐Salas, Saeed Amirjalayer, Frank Glorius, Harry Mönig
pmc-13361271.description: Atomic step‐edges on metallic surfaces are highly active catalytic sites due to their reduced coordination and modified electronic structure. Yet, approaches to organic ligand functionalization on the single‐molecule level have largely targeted flat terrace geometries, whereas site‐specific step‐edge functionalization remains unaddressed.

pmc-13589536.title: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Potential of Plant-Derived Exosome-Like Nanovesicles in Skin Tissue Regeneration
pmc-13589536.creator: Xiaomeng Ma, Jiayu Shi, Ruifang Li, Wenjie Hu, Kun Li, Le Zhao, Min Wang
pmc-13589536.description: The integrity of the skin barrier is paramount for human physiological homeostasis. Recently, plant-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (PENs) lipid bilayer nanostructures inherently enriched with diverse natural bioactive cargos have emerged as transformative nanotherapeutic platforms. Compared to conventional mammalian and microbial-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), PENs offer distinct clinical translation advantages.
